author: Meridian Church Newswire
title: Hastening: A Weekly Church Report - Meridian Magazine
text:
This week brings inspiring stories of temple growth, Christ-centered experiences, service, and faith in action. President Dallin H. Oaks dedicates the Belo Horizonte Brazil Temple, while exciting new experiences prepare to welcome guests to Temple Square. Thousands of young adults gather “Together in Christ,” and seminary and institute enrollment reaches more than 1 million worldwide. Across the globe, Church members are lending helping hands after the Kumamoto earthquake, while new temple milestones unfold in Huntsville, San Diego and Cleveland. Plus, a thought-provoking look at the surprising connection between religious faith and physical health.
ONE
Centered on Christ, Built for Eternity: President Oaks Dedicates Brazil Temple
Sunday, August 16, 2026
Temples Rising
President Dallin H. Oaks dedicated the Belo Horizonte Brazil Temple on Sunday, August 16, 2026. This is the Church’s 12th dedicated temple in Brazil and 220th operating temple worldwide. This was the prophet’s first trip outside the United States as President of the Church. In interviews the previous day with Church Newsroom staff and Brazilian journalist Leandro Magalhães , President Oaks reflected on why he selected Brazil for his first temple dedication outside the U.S. READ STORY HERE .
TWO
Step Inside the Story of Christ: New Experiences Coming to Temple Square
Monday, August 17, 2026
Salt Lake Temple
New experiences are coming to Temple Square in the coming months. These experiences will be available for Temple Square guests before, during and after the Salt Lake Temple Celebration . These include experiences in the Joseph Smith Memorial Building, exhibits in the Conference Center and projections on the Salt Lake Tabernacle’s iconic domed ceiling. READ STORY HERE .
THREE
The Power of a Friend, the Strength of Faith: Young Adults Gather “Together in Christ”
Saturday, August 15, 2026
Chosen Generation
For the fourth year in a row, thousands of young single adults (YSAs) converged on downtown Salt Lake City, Utah, for the Utah Area Young Single Adult Conference on Friday and Saturday, August 14–15, 2026. The young adults, ranging in age from 18 to 35, came to the Salt Palace Convention Center to learn from leaders from The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and other speakers, attend classes, participate in service projects and build friendships with others. READ STORY HERE .
FOUR
After the Ground Shook, Helping Hands Reached Out Across Kumamoto
Friday, August 14, 2026
Humanitarian Outreach
At approximately 4:27 p.m. on July 28, 2026, a powerful earthquake measuring magnitude 7.1 struck central Kumamoto Prefecture, registering a maximum seismic intensity of 7 on Japan’s seismic scale. The disaster, known as the 2026 Kumamoto earthquake, has left nearly 4,000 people living in evacuation shelters, while more than 28,000 homes have been destroyed, severely damaged, or partially damaged. READ STORY HERE.
FIVE
One Invitation at a Time, 85,000 Friends Join Seminary and Institute
Wednesday, August 12, 2026
Chosen Generation
Worldwide enrollment in the seminary and institute programs of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints now exceeds 1,090,000, including 85,695 friends of other faiths, whose enrollment has nearly doubled in the past two years. Behind that growth is a simple act: one person inviting another. READ STORY HERE .
SIX
A House of Peace and Hope: Construction Begins on the Huntsville Alabama Temple
Saturday, August 15, 2026
Temples Rising
A groundbreaking ceremony was held for the Huntsville Alabama Temple of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on Saturday, August 15, 2026. Elder John D. Amos of the United States Southeast Area Presidency presided at the event, offering the dedicatory prayer on the future temple site. READ STORY AND SEE PHOTOS HERE .
SEVEN
A Temple’s Story, Renewed: President Christofferson to Rededicate San Diego California Temple
Tuesday, August 18, 2026
Temples Rising
President D. Todd Christofferson, Second Counselor in the First Presidency of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, will rededicate the San Diego California Temple on Sunday, August 23, 2026. The temple, which closed in 2023 for extensive renovation, will be rededicated. WATCH VIDEO OF THE TEMPLE’S HISTORY HERE .
EIGHT
From Kirtland to Cleveland: A New Temple Continues Ohio’s Restoration Story
Sunday, August 16, 2026
Temples Rising
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles dedicated the Cleveland Ohio Temple of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on Sunday, August 16, 2026. The Cleveland Ohio Temple is located in northeastern Ohio about 20 miles southwest of the historic Kirtland Temple, which was dedicated in 1836 but is now one of the Church’s historic sites open for daily tours to the public. READ STORY HERE .
NINE
The Physical Health Case for Religion
Monday, August 10, 2026
In The News
There is a resource, strongly tied to a longer and healthier life, that our health system rarely acknowledges. The United States spends more per person on health care than any other nation, yet Americans live shorter lives than people in nearly every other developed nation. A 2025 Lancet analysis found the United States has made unusually poor progress against chronic disease, with mortality rising among adults ages 20 through 45—the same generations now least connected to religious communities. These data should make us curious. Are there “model” groups or best practices that yield significantly better health results that we should consider? READ STORY HERE .
